headline: Highest risk is data leakage: Windsurf’s broad filesystem/network access can expose workspace content while Opik has broad network egress and REST API access, creating a plausible cross-agent leak path.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Windsurf can read clipboard and workspace files and use MCP servers, so it may ingest content from Opik if Opik’s outputs are copied into shared files or prompts. Opik itself is an observability/evaluation tool with REST API output, so the interaction is indirect rather than a proven shared channel. Uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF Opik outputs are copied into a Windsurf-opened file or clipboard, Windsurf may treat that content as instructions.
IF Windsurf is connected to an MCP server that forwards Opik output, prompt injection becomes reachable.
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based handoff between tools.
Keep Opik outputs in read-only files.
Use separate workspaces for each agent.
Require manual review before Windsurf acts on copied content.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for inter-agent content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Windsurf reads workspace files, uses broad network egress, and handles open files; Opik also has broad network egress and REST API access. That creates a plausible path for workspace content to leave the local environment through either agent, even though no shared filesystem is explicitly documented for Opik. Because the pairwise leak path is inferred, not directly evidenced, medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF the same sensitive files are opened in Windsurf and then summarized or exported by Opik, those contents can leak.
IF Windsurf is configured to send file context to remote services, workspace data may leave the host.
mitigations: Do not open sensitive files in Windsurf.
Use a separate non-sensitive workspace for Opik.
Turn off any remote sync or export path.
Restrict network access at the host firewall.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Windsurf can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses; Opik has broad network egress and REST API access. If both operate on the same repo or workspace, concurrent writes and git mutations can conflict, and Windsurf’s per-window shared state via local filesystem increases collision risk. The overlap is directly supported by both profiles.
conditions: IF both agents target the same git checkout, concurrent edits can overwrite each other.
IF Opik writes artifacts while Windsurf auto-executes commands, filesystem races can occur.
mitigations: Use separate branches per agent.
Lock the workspace before either agent writes.
Disable auto-execute in Windsurf.
Keep Opik read-only when Windsurf is active.
requires-engineering: add file-locking or orchestration around shared repos.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Windsurf can act on files and commands, so if it consumes Opik-generated summaries or evaluations as authoritative, errors can cascade into edits or actions. Opik’s REST API output can become an upstream source, but there is no direct evidence that it is blindly trusted by default. The pathway exists, but verification is not documented.
conditions: IF Windsurf uses Opik output as a source of truth without review, incorrect facts can propagate into code or commands.
IF Opik emits malformed evaluations and Windsurf auto-applies them, downstream errors can cascade.
mitigations: Require human review of Opik outputs.
Disable Windsurf auto-execute.
Add a verification step before file writes.
Keep Opik outputs separate from actionable prompts.
requires-engineering: add schema validation for inter-agent handoffs.

E_compliance.rationale: Opik is open-source and only documented here as broad-network REST tooling, while Windsurf is closed-source, runs as the user, and handles model provider keys and workspace files. No explicit residency or regulated-data mismatch is documented, so only a low compliance concern is supportable from the profiles. The other agent is cited because the risk is about their combined handling of workspace data.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Windsurf workspace files, compliance review is required.
IF Opik exports those files to a remote service, retention and residency controls must be checked.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared workspaces.
Review vendor data-processing terms.
Separate sensitive and non-sensitive projects.
Disable optional key sharing.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls.
